sections.title: Parallel work and exclusive ownership
sections.body:
After M0, A, B and C can edit, run focused tests and prepare PRs concurrently. Each gets a separate native issue, branch `feature/issue-<number>-ui-tests-<area>` and fresh managed worktree from the coordinator’s exact approved base SHA. Prefer the app worktree tool; if this collection context cannot create one, use `git worktree add` in the actual monorepo. Never reuse an occupied checkout.

| Session | Exclusive editable area | Suggested worktree | Optional dev/HMR ports |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: Git/Issues | `apps/openape-git/**` | `ui-tests-git` | 5481 / 5491 |
| B: Inbox/PWA | `apps/openape-pods-relay/**` | `ui-tests-inbox` | 5482 / 5492 |
| C: Reports | `apps/openape-testrun/**` | `ui-tests-reports` | 5483 / 5493 |

The coordinator alone owns root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `turbo.json`, `.openape/checks.json`, hooks, shared scripts, root AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING, generated architecture docs, `docs/agents/active-work.md` and this plan. Shared packages/modules and `apps/openape-pods/**` are reference-only for area sessions. No shared file is silently claimed. Request a coordinator patch or revise scope if one is needed.

Each session may update its existing area test config and docs. Dependency additions and manifest script changes must be agreed during M0 so the coordinator can reconcile the lockfile/generated map. Plan sources are read-only for area sessions; they provide a handoff, not concurrent edits to the same Plan. The user follows the separate chats; the coordinator reads their status from here.

sections.title: Isolation and shared Mac capacity
sections.body:
Every worktree has its own install, build outputs, Vite/Turbo artifacts, synthetic database, test HOME and browser profile. Do not symlink another checkout’s `node_modules`, `.nuxt`, `dist`, `.output` or writable fixtures. Existing package-download caches may be shared. Use the pinned toolchain in every shell:

```sh
export OPENAPE_PNPM_BIN=/Users/patrickhofmann/Companies/private/repos/openape/.toolchains/pnpm/10.29.3/bin
export PATH="$OPENAPE_PNPM_BIN:$PATH"
. ./scripts/activate-node.sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm run doctor
```

If doctor reports missing prerequisite builds, run the selected checkout’s documented prebuild and recheck; do not use another checkout’s outputs. Confirm reserved ports are free; fail on collisions, never kill another session’s process. Existing integration fixtures should allocate their own ephemeral ports and temporary data.

Focused tests can run concurrently with bounded workers. Full affected gates, cold full builds and real integration acceptance share one heavy-check slot on this Mac. The coordinator grants that slot to one session at a time, recording chat/worktree/command and release status in its launch ledger. A busy session continues independent work. No shell polling loop, timeout inflation, global process kill or hook bypass. Repository-wide Vitest uses the established `TURBO_ENV_MODE=loose VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1` invocation where needed; focused package commands choose a small explicit cap. Record settings with measurements. Worktrees permit parallel development, not unlimited machine capacity.

sections.title: Area tasks and boundaries that stay real
sections.body:
### A — Git/Issues
Start at `e2e/issues.layout.test.ts`, `e2e/fixture.ts`, `tests/issue-ui.test.ts`, `app/components/Issue*.vue` and `app/assets/main.css`. The layout suite currently starts the app and IdP. Build a browser-component route through the existing Vitest infrastructure using real Nuxt UI controls and generated production CSS. Reuse existing scenarios for creation, Markdown preview, comments, filtering, triage, draft/error/conflict states and narrow layouts. Introduce a small boundary adapter only where needed; avoid a broad app refactor. Keep real login/callback, server permissions, durable create/comment behavior, migration/download protection and representative route wiring. Do not label mocked Markdown as proof of server sanitization.

### B — Inbox/PWA
Start at `e2e/inbox-app.test.ts`, existing `test/inbox-{decision,list,item,client,worker}.test.ts` and `app/components/Inbox*.vue`. Separate card presentation, sender/classification, tags, evidence-required forms, pending/accepted/applied states, undo, empty/error and narrow/dark presentation from the large integrated scenario. Use real components, styles and a deterministic transport boundary. Preserve real service-worker registration/cache behavior, offline/reconnect, restart/reinstall, cross-account separation, real authentication and decision receipt/application semantics. Do not modify the shared Pods renderer; coordinate a dependency request if necessary.

### C — Reports
Start at `vitest.browser.config.ts`, `tests/layout/setup.ts`, `tests/layout/*.test.ts`, `app/components/DocumentReport.vue` and `app/assets/main.css`. Upgrade existing browser tests to load the actual stylesheet pipeline; replace the partial hand-written preflight without hiding component regressions. Cover the meaningful report shell, series/version navigation, document/briefing views, screenshot frames and responsive errors using existing scenarios. Keep real publication/CLI round trips, private access and expiry, content-origin isolation, CSP and actual iframe behavior in their appropriate integration/security tests. A sandbox attribute assertion alone does not replace browser isolation evidence.

IdP and `nuxt-auth-sp` are read-only pattern references. Tasks/CRM remain optional subsequent work, requiring a concrete UI need and a scope decision. Troop has no session, acceptance item or dependency in this plan.

sections.title: Launch packet and integration protocol
sections.body:
The coordinator creates each user-owned chat only after the launch request. Fill in the actual approved Plan URL/revision, frozen base SHA, native issue, branch, absolute worktree, area, ports and allowed paths. Attach the relevant area section and these shared instructions:

> Implement only your assigned area of approved Plan revision 1. Read this checkout’s AGENTS and mapped memory rules. Verify branch/base/status; preserve other worktrees. Use the existing test infrastructure and real production components/CSS. Inventory old assertions and retained boundaries before editing. Do not edit coordinator-owned files, other areas or the Plan. Raise shared dependency needs in your handoff. Run focused checks, demonstrate replacement failures, inspect screenshots and publish actual evidence. Obtain the coordinator’s heavy-check slot before full gates/builds/integration acceptance. Commit/push normally, open a native PR and link the area issue. Leave the PR open for coordinated review/merge. Return issue/PR, source/base SHA, touched paths, exact results, assertion mapping, evidence URL, remaining risks, processes/ports and resource-slot state. Do not message other chats without Patrick’s explicit authorization.

During launch, ask for/record explicit authorization for the coordinator to send operational messages to the three chats. Reads and progress monitoring stay in this parent chat. Do not spawn hidden implementation agents as a substitute for the requested sessions.

Area handoffs live in their own existing testing document or `docs/ui-test-migration.md` beneath the owned app. The coordinator maintains one launch ledger under `.claude/plans/ui-test-migration/` and the single published Plan; preserve the current Reports version on updates. Native issues track implementation, the Plan tracks proposal/approval, PRs track code review. Link them without copying all status into each system.

Merge one PR at a time against reviewed source and target SHAs. Prefer Git/Issues first as the pattern reference, but an independent ready area need not wait. Inspect newly merged main changes, including the separate legacy extraction. Merge main into the owned feature branch if integration needs changes; do not rewrite already mirrored history. Rerun checks affected by the new source/dependencies and retain exact evidence. Cross-cutting repairs go through the coordinator. After each merge, record the receipt and close only its completed technical issue. Roll back a faulty area through a revert PR preserving unrelated areas; restore original assertions before retiring a replacement.

verification: For every moved assertion record old test, observable contract, replacement test, retained boundary and a targeted counter-proof. Temporarily break the relevant behavior/style, observe failure, restore it and rerun. Keep only useful regressions.

Use real production components and stylesheet entry points, including Tailwind/Nuxt UI generation and fonts/tokens where relevant. Do not copy CSS fixes into setup or replace the measured UI controls with stubs.

Capture representative wide/narrow, light/dark, loading/empty/error states where applicable. Inspect the actual images and publish a private Test Run with exact SHA, commands, timings, mapping and limitations.

Measure the old and new relevant commands on the same machine with declared cold/warm cache and worker settings, outside competing heavy checks. Include startup cost. Do not invent a percentage target or treat fewer assertions as a speedup.

Run focused checks during editing; normal pre-push affected unit gates once per pushed head, plus relevant explicit browser/integration acceptance. Keep CI paused. Record pre-existing failures and never turn skips into passes.

risks.title: False confidence from simulated backends
risks.mitigation: UI tests prove presentation and requests, not actual authorization or durable effects. Retain API/adapter contracts and representative real journeys.

risks.title: Worktree isolation does not isolate ports, resources or shared files
risks.mitigation: Enforce path ownership, isolated installs/artifacts/profiles, reserved ports and one heavy-check slot. Centralize lockfile changes and merges.

risks.title: Concurrent legacy extraction changes dependencies
risks.mitigation: Exclude Troop. Refresh and inspect the extraction’s merged changes at preparation and integration. Request only the specific shared dependency clarification if needed; never edit or reset its worktree.

Start at `vitest.browser.config.ts`, `tests/layout/setup.ts`, `tests/layout/*.test.ts`, `app/components/DocumentReport.vue` and `app/assets/main.css`. Upgrade existing browser tests to load the actual stylesheet pipeline; replace the partial hand-written preflight without hiding component regressions. Cover the meaningful report shell, series/version navigation, document/briefing views, screenshot frames and responsive errors using existing scenarios. Keep real publication/CLI round trips, private access and expiry, content-origin isolation, CSP and actual iframe behavior in their appropriate integration/security tests. A sandbox attribute assertion alone does not replace browser isolation evidence.

IdP and `nuxt-auth-sp` are read-only pattern references. Tasks/CRM remain optional subsequent work, requiring a concrete UI need and a scope decision. Troop has no session, acceptance item or dependency in this plan.
entries.text:
### A — Git/Issues
Einstieg über `e2e/issues.layout.test.ts`, `e2e/fixture.ts`, `tests/issue-ui.test.ts`, `app/components/Issue*.vue` und `app/assets/main.css`. Die Layout-Suite startet derzeit Anwendung und IdP. In der vorhandenen Vitest-Infrastruktur Browser-Komponententests mit echten Nuxt-UI-Steuerelementen und erzeugtem Produktions-CSS aufbauen. Bestehende Szenarien für Erstellung, Markdown-Vorschau, Kommentare, Filter, Triage, Entwurfs-/Fehler-/Konfliktzustände und schmale Layouts wiederverwenden. Nur bei Bedarf einen kleinen Schnittstellenadapter einführen; keinen breiten App-Umbau. Echten Login/Callback, serverseitige Rechte, dauerhafte Erstellung/Kommentare, Migrations-/Downloadschutz und repräsentative Routenanbindung erhalten. Simuliertes Markdown beweist keine serverseitige Bereinigung.

### B — Inbox/PWA
Einstieg über `e2e/inbox-app.test.ts`, vorhandene `test/inbox-{decision,list,item,client,worker}.test.ts` und `app/components/Inbox*.vue`. Kartendarstellung, Absender/Klassifikation, Tags, Nachweis-Pflichtfelder, wartende/angenommene/angewendete Zustände, Rückgängig, Leer-/Fehlerzustände und schmale/dunkle Darstellung aus dem großen Integrationsszenario lösen. Echte Komponenten, Styles und eine deterministische Transportschnittstelle verwenden. Echte Service-Worker-Registrierung und Caches, Offlinebetrieb/Wiederverbindung, Neustart/Neuinstallation, Kontentrennung, Authentifizierung und Entscheidungsannahme/-anwendung erhalten. Den gemeinsamen Pods-Renderer nicht ändern; nötige Abhängigkeiten mit der Koordination klären.

### C — Reports
Einstieg über `vitest.browser.config.ts`, `tests/layout/setup.ts`, `tests/layout/*.test.ts`, `app/components/DocumentReport.vue` und `app/assets/main.css`. Vorhandene Browsertests auf die tatsächliche Stylesheet-Verarbeitung umstellen; den teilweise nachgebauten Preflight ersetzen, ohne Komponentenregressionen zu verdecken. Relevanten Berichtsrahmen, Serien-/Versionsnavigation, Dokument-/Briefingansichten, Screenshot-Rahmen und responsive Fehler mit bestehenden Szenarien abdecken. Echte Veröffentlichungs-/CLI-Abläufe, privaten Zugriff und Ablauf, Isolation der Inhalts-Origin, CSP und tatsächliches iframe-Verhalten in passenden Integrations-/Sicherheitstests erhalten. Eine Prüfung des Sandbox-Attributs allein ersetzt keinen Nachweis der Browserisolation.

IdP und `nuxt-auth-sp` dienen nur als gelesene Musterreferenzen. Tasks/CRM bleiben optionale spätere Arbeit mit konkretem UI-Bedarf und eigener Umfangsentscheidung. Troop erhält in diesem Plan weder Session noch Abnahmepunkt oder Abhängigkeit.

entries.source:
The coordinator creates each user-owned chat only after the launch request. Fill in the actual approved Plan URL/revision, frozen base SHA, native issue, branch, absolute worktree, area, ports and allowed paths. Attach the relevant area section and these shared instructions:

> Implement only your assigned area of approved Plan revision 1. Read this checkout’s AGENTS and mapped memory rules. Verify branch/base/status; preserve other worktrees. Use the existing test infrastructure and real production components/CSS. Inventory old assertions and retained boundaries before editing. Do not edit coordinator-owned files, other areas or the Plan. Raise shared dependency needs in your handoff. Run focused checks, demonstrate replacement failures, inspect screenshots and publish actual evidence. Obtain the coordinator’s heavy-check slot before full gates/builds/integration acceptance. Commit/push normally, open a native PR and link the area issue. Leave the PR open for coordinated review/merge. Return issue/PR, source/base SHA, touched paths, exact results, assertion mapping, evidence URL, remaining risks, processes/ports and resource-slot state. Do not message other chats without Patrick’s explicit authorization.

During launch, ask for/record explicit authorization for the coordinator to send operational messages to the three chats. Reads and progress monitoring stay in this parent chat. Do not spawn hidden implementation agents as a substitute for the requested sessions.

Area handoffs live in their own existing testing document or `docs/ui-test-migration.md` beneath the owned app. The coordinator maintains one launch ledger under `.claude/plans/ui-test-migration/` and the single published Plan; preserve the current Reports version on updates. Native issues track implementation, the Plan tracks proposal/approval, PRs track code review. Link them without copying all status into each system.

Merge one PR at a time against reviewed source and target SHAs. Prefer Git/Issues first as the pattern reference, but an independent ready area need not wait. Inspect newly merged main changes, including the separate legacy extraction. Merge main into the owned feature branch if integration needs changes; do not rewrite already mirrored history. Rerun checks affected by the new source/dependencies and retain exact evidence. Cross-cutting repairs go through the coordinator. After each merge, record the receipt and close only its completed technical issue. Roll back a faulty area through a revert PR preserving unrelated areas; restore original assertions before retiring a replacement.
entries.text:
Die Koordination erstellt jeden nutzereigenen Chat erst nach dem Startauftrag. Tatsächliche freigegebene Plan-URL/Revision, feste Basis-SHA, natives Issue, Branch, absoluten Worktree, Bereich, Ports und erlaubte Pfade einsetzen. Den passenden Bereichsabschnitt und diese gemeinsamen Anweisungen übergeben:

> Setze nur deinen zugewiesenen Bereich der freigegebenen Planrevision 1 um. Lies AGENTS dieses Checkouts und die zugeordneten Wissensregeln. Prüfe Branch, Basis und Status; erhalte fremde Worktrees. Nutze die bestehende Testinfrastruktur und echte Produktionskomponenten samt CSS. Erfasse vor Änderungen alte Assertions und zu erhaltende Systemgrenzen. Bearbeite keine Dateien der Koordination, fremden Bereiche oder des Plans. Melde gemeinsame Abhängigkeiten in deiner Übergabe. Prüfe gezielt, belege das Fehlschlagen der Ersatztests, sieh Screenshots an und veröffentliche tatsächliche Nachweise. Hole vor Vollgates/Builds/Integrationsabnahmen den Slot der Koordination für aufwendige Prüfungen. Committe und pushe regulär, eröffne einen nativen PR und verknüpfe das Bereichsissue. Lass den PR für koordinierte Prüfung und Zusammenführung offen. Liefere Issue/PR, Quell-/Basis-SHA, geänderte Pfade, genaue Ergebnisse, Assertion-Zuordnung, Nachweis-URL, offene Risiken, Prozesse/Ports und Slotstatus. Sende ohne Patricks ausdrückliche Autorisierung keine Nachrichten an andere Chats.

Beim Start ausdrückliche Autorisierung für operative Nachrichten der Koordination an die drei Chats einholen beziehungsweise festhalten. Lesen und Fortschrittskontrolle bleiben in diesem übergeordneten Chat. Keine versteckten Umsetzungsagenten als Ersatz für die gewünschten Sessions starten.

Bereichsübergaben liegen in der eigenen vorhandenen Testdokumentation oder in `docs/ui-test-migration.md` unter der zuständigen App. Die Koordination pflegt eine Startübersicht unter `.claude/plans/ui-test-migration/` und den einzigen veröffentlichten Plan; bei Aktualisierungen die aktuelle Reports-Version berücksichtigen. Native Issues führen Umsetzung, der Plan führt Vorschlag/Freigabe, PRs führen Codereview. Verknüpfen, ohne sämtliche Statusdaten in jedes System zu kopieren.

Jeweils einen PR gegen geprüfte Quell- und Ziel-SHAs zusammenführen. Git/Issues als Muster möglichst zuerst, aber ein unabhängiger fertiger Bereich muss nicht warten. Neue main-Änderungen einschließlich der separaten Legacy-Ausgliederung prüfen. Wenn die Integration Änderungen erfordert, main in den eigenen Featurebranch mergen; bereits gespiegelte Historie nicht umschreiben. Von neuer Quelle oder Abhängigkeiten betroffene Prüfungen erneut ausführen und genaue Nachweise erhalten. Bereichsübergreifende Reparaturen übernimmt die Koordination. Nach jedem Merge den Beleg festhalten und nur das abgeschlossene technische Issue schließen. Einen fehlerhaften Bereich per Revert-PR zurücknehmen, ohne andere Bereiche anzutasten; ursprüngliche Assertions wiederherstellen, bevor ein Ersatz entfernt wird.

Der verifizierte Nachweis umfasst 13 Browserfälle, 12 erhaltene reale Integrationsfälle, 197 Unit-Tests und den Produktionsbuild. Inbox/PWA besteht 14 Browserfälle und 48 gezielte Unit-Tests mit unverändertem Produktions-CSS; finale reale Abnahme und Push stehen noch aus. Reports hält den Slot für Produktionsbuild und erhaltene Integrationsabnahme. Alle Bereiche dokumentieren Startbasis 95d1083a und gemeinsamen Fixture-Stand b248ac15. Zentrale Dokumentation wird mit den verbleibenden Implementierungs-PRs integriert; tatsächliche finale Merge-Belege und Abschluss werden in diesem veröffentlichten Plan und den nativen Issues festgehalten. Troop bleibt ausgeschlossen; kein Deployment und keine CI-Aktivierung. Das zusätzliche Opus-Review war wegen einer abgelaufenen OAuth-Sitzung nicht verfügbar.
